figures.alt_text: Two separate horizontal stacked bars. The upper bar shows that 88.61 percent of asthma GWAS discovery individuals sit in the European category. The lower bar shows Loudoun County residents by self-identified race, a different measurement of a different population.
figures.caption: Upper panel: initial-stage discovery individuals across the asthma studies in GWAS Catalog release 2026-11-02, by the catalog's broad ancestral category. Lower panel: Loudoun County residents by self-identified race, ACS 2024 5-year estimates (acs/acs5), table B02001. ACS categories are self-identified race and ethnicity, which are social categories and not genetic ancestry. They are shown only to describe the population the atlas is meant to serve. The two panels have separate axes and are not comparable: one counts people enrolled in studies and groups them by genetic ancestry, the other counts residents and groups them by a social category.
figures.limitation: Descriptive only, and not an effect estimate: these are counts of people enrolled and associations declared, and v1 computes no cross-ancestry gene-environment effect (CONTEXT.md X7). The discovery composition is the composition of the published evidence base, not of any population: a category with few individuals means the evidence was measured in few people from it, which is a property of who was studied and not of anyone's genome. Because the asthma evidence base is predominantly European, every locus count here rests mostly on European-ancestry discovery samples, and findings from that base transfer unevenly to other groups. A study sample naming several broad ancestral categories is split equally across them, because the catalog publishes no per-category count within a row. The discovery total is a sum of study sample sizes and not a headcount: asthma studies draw repeatedly on the same cohorts, so a participant in several studies is counted once per study. ACS categories are self-identified race and ethnicity, which are social categories and not genetic ancestry. They are shown only to describe the population the atlas is meant to serve.
figures.title: Who the asthma GWAS evidence was measured in, and who lives in Loudoun County
